solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What gives the impression Susan's legs must be tanned?

definitions.text: What gives the impression Susan's legs must be tanned?

indicators.note: to tan someone is to give them a beating, and a beaten-up phrase has its letters knocked into a new order

parts.note: the name with its apostrophe-s and the following word, ten letters in all

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what could make Susan's legs look as if she has a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: tinted lenses make everything, Susan's legs included, look browner than it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinted spectacles darken the view, so the wearer sees pale skin as if it had caught the sun.

clue.text: Suffer little Albert's position in goal?

parts.note: surface reading: where a small boy called Albert stands when playing in goal
setter's reading: little Albert is the short name Al; written down the column, the word goal has those two letters sitting beneath its first two

explanation.surface: A child called Albert has to put up with being stuck in goal.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry GOAL is written top to bottom, so AL lies under GO: describe that position and you have the answer, which also means Suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or endure it, usually something unpleasant, so it is a synonym of suffer.

clue.text: Little indication genetically modified grassland is spreading

indicators.note: the outer pair of letters spreads itself out to make room for something in between

parts.note: the standard abbreviation, as in GM crops
a lea is a meadow, a common crossword word

explanation.surface: A faint sign that genetically modified crops are creeping across the pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam of hope is a faint sign or trace of it, so a gleam is a small indication.

clue.text: Business park cooks doling out fancy buns for evening's entertainment

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, so what is left is rearranged
doling out means handing over, so those letters leave the phrase they are taken from
the letters to be removed are themselves jumbled, so they are taken out wherever they lie rather than as one run

parts.note: taken as written
the letters to be removed, in any order

explanation.surface: Bakers on an industrial estate hand out fancy buns as the night's entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove B, U, N and S from BUSINESSPARK to leave IESSPARK, then rearrange those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Après-ski is the socialising that follows a day on the slopes, the evening's fun at a ski resort.

clue.text: He's going to rally desperate junkies meeting here

indicators.note: something desperate is wild and out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A man sets out to gather a crowd of desperate addicts.
explanation.walkthrough: Beyond the fairground stall, the phrase is slang for a place where drug users gather to inject.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a shooting gallery is a den where addicts meet to inject drugs, to shoot up being to inject.

clue.text: Regression of 50% of language is notable

indicators.note: a regression is a going back, so the string is read from the other end
half of the word language is kept, namely its first four letters

parts.note: the first half of the eight-letter word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A linguist observes that a language falling back by half is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: LANG and IS together are written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means conspicuous or remarkable, as in a signal achievement, so it matches notable.

clue.text: Thousands beseiging University College? Rubbish

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: two different symbols for a thousand: M, the Roman numeral, and K, as in kilo
U and C are the standard abbreviations, as in UCL

explanation.surface: Crowds besiege a university college, and someone dismisses the protest as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Muck is dirt or filth, and figuratively worthless stuff, so it is a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Drink carried by two-thirds of clergymen — something short

indicators.note: what is carried sits inside its carrier
only six of the nine letters of the following word are kept

parts.note: clergymen are ministers, and two-thirds of that nine-letter word is its first six letters
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A drink is handed round by a couple of vicars, and something brief follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like a description of the drink, a spirit measure, but it is the definition of a skimpy garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniskirt is a very short skirt, so it is literally a garment that is something short.

clue.text: Sack of money? That's right

parts.note: cash is money
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a bag of cash and asks whether it is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bank teller, but here the word is the verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to discharge them from service in disgrace, the same as to sack them.

clue.text: Border guards exposed

indicators.note: something exposed has had its covering stripped off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: to hedge is to protect or guard against, as in hedging a bet

explanation.surface: Guards stationed on a frontier are left in an unprotected position.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the first and last letters off HEDGES.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the boundary or margin of something, so it is a synonym of border.

clue.text: Rationalise Byzantine orangeries

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to streamline an elaborate set of glasshouses for citrus trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To rationalise a business is to restructure it for efficiency, which is to reorganise it.

clue.text: So little to eat? I'm astonished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tiny fragments of bread or cake, a meagre meal
second meaning: an exclamation of surprise

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one shocked diner; the question and the exclamation are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural of a small fragment of food and a mild British interjection expressing surprise.

clue.text: Stun Asterix's sex change surgeon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold someone motionless with shock
second meaning, whimsical: Asterix characters have names ending -ix, like the druid Getafix, so a gender surgeon there might be named for what he fixes

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented name: in the Asterix comics every Gaul's name ends in -ix, so the joke splits the answer into trans and fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfix someone is to make them motionless with astonishment or horror, much as a stunning blow would.

clue.text: Hide spy's family

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, here with the possessive S
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A secret agent's relatives go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide looks like a verb in the spy story, but it is the noun for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Moleskin is the pelt of a mole, or a heavy cotton cloth imitating it, so it is a kind of hide.

clue.text: Better to avoid extremes… keeping quiet when one's out of order?

definitions.text: Better to avoid extremes… keeping quiet when one's out of order?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
out of order means not in sequence, so the letters of the word quiet are shifted
avoiding the extremes means dropping the first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; its one (I) moves

explanation.surface: Advice that it is best to stay moderate and silent when you are in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: One is the Roman numeral I, which moves to the front of the word it belongs to. Read whole, the clue describes good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite conduct, which recommends restraint and silence rather than behaving improperly.

clue.text: Drugstore straddling main road

indicators.note: the word sits astride the gap between two clue words, part in each

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A pharmacy sits across both sides of a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: An inro is a small Japanese lacquered box hung from the sash, used to carry medicines; a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Since an inro was traditionally a container for medicines, the setter calls it, whimsically, a store of drugs.

clue.text: What's common to Obama and Biden leaves Bush in high spirits

indicators.note: the letter leaves, departing from the word it was in

parts.note: euphorbia is a spurge, a shrub or bush

parts.words: What's common to Obama and Biden
parts.note: the only letter that appears in both surnames

explanation.surface: Something shared by two Democratic presidents drives a Republican one into high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the president, but it is a plant; take B out of EUPHORBIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a feeling of intense happiness or elation, which is what being in high spirits means.

clue.text: Remove skins from huge olid fruit

indicators.note: peeling off the skins leaves only the inner flesh of each word

parts.note: the two inner letters
the two inner letters; olid means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: Peel a huge, stinking piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo hybrid with a wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Boat house overwhelmed by four pints of liquid nitrogen

indicators.note: what is overwhelmed is swamped and engulfed by what surrounds it

parts.note: GAL is the abbreviation of gallon; strictly four pints is half a gallon
Leo is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A houseboat is swamped by a few pints of liquid nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: Boat house reads as one thing but splits into definition and wordplay. Four pints is really half a gallon, so the GAL is slightly loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the 15th to 17th centuries, so it is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Luvvie initially choked by Canal+ award for over-indulgence

indicators.note: something choked has another thing tight around its neck

parts.note: the gut is the alimentary canal

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter; a luvvie is an affected actor
a Tony is the Broadway theatre award

explanation.surface: A theatrical type chokes up while receiving a prize from the French TV channel Canal+.
explanation.walkthrough: Canal+ is a French broadcaster, but here the plus sign simply means 'followed by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is the habit of eating to excess, one of the seven deadly sins, so it is over-indulgence.

clue.text: More unpleasant new wine about to be served up

parts.note: standard abbreviation for new
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

indicators.note: in a down entry, serving up lifts the word so it reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cheap new wine is about to be poured, to the diners' disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, so it means more unpleasant.

clue.text: Bound to involve 'arry's woman in rows

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in and wrap it up inside

parts.note: bound with rope is tied
the word her with the H dropped, as a Cockney like 'Arry would say it

explanation.surface: A Cockney man's partner is bound to end up quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Rows suggests arguments, but the definition means arranged in tiers. Cockney speakers drop their aitches, hence the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered describes seating or layers set one above another in ranks, which is arranged in rows.

clue.text: Entirely uniform container of mineral-rich soil

parts.note: all means wholly or entirely
Uniform is the NATO alphabet word for U
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: An unchanging pot of fertile earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Of belongs to the definition, which describes something made of alluvium.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluvial means made of or relating to alluvium, the fertile sediment deposited by rivers.

clue.text: The ultimate in transport? It carries a stiff charge

definitions.text: The ultimate in transport? It carries a stiff charge

parts.note: surface reading: the very best kind of travel; setter's reading: the last vehicle anyone rides in
surface reading: it costs a lot; setter's reading: its charge, or load, is a stiff, slang for a corpse

explanation.walkthrough: Ultimate means final rather than finest, and a stiff is a dead body rather than a hefty fee.
explanation.definitionFit: This vehicle carries a coffin to the funeral, the final journey a person makes.

clue.text: Allow lunatic to defer start of meaningful relations

indicators.note: deferring the start means the first letter is postponed to the end of the word

parts.note: a lunatic is mad
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A crazy person is permitted to postpone the start of a serious relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: MAD with its M moved to the end becomes ADM.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, and to admit a point is to allow it.

clue.text: Yankee confused Terry with ease in the past

definitions.note: a noun meaning the past; 'in the past' reads like 'of yesteryear'

parts.note: Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y

indicators.note: confused words are muddled up, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the name and the noun together, with as the joining word

explanation.surface: An American bewildered Terry with how easily he managed things long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means the past, especially remembered with nostalgia, as in the stars of yesteryear.

clue.text: Return morning papers to Abigail?

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for morning is read backwards

parts.note: a.m. is morning
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand the morning newspapers back to a woman named Abigail.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, after a waiting-woman in Beaumont and Fletcher's play The Scornful Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail became a generic term for a lady's maid, so the name stands for the servant.

clue.text: Joint leaders of expensive enterprise needing key backing

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the collected letters read from the end
leaders are those at the front, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Founders of a costly business need a crucial backer to share the venture.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge between thigh and lower leg, a joint of the body.

clue.text: Director extremely wise, according to auditors, to limit striker's power base

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters of the word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: to limit is to bound something on both sides
auditors are listeners, so the word is taken as it sounds rather than as written

parts.note: said out loud, the word sounds like Ys, the plural of the letter Y
a batter strikes the ball in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A shrewd manager takes care to keep his top goal-scorer's influence in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Striker suggests a football forward, but here it is the batsman; the two letters from the sound of wise go one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry battery is a cell with paste electrolyte, the base source of power in a torch or radio.
